definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese percussion instrument made from a wooden body with animal skin stretched over both ends. Used in festivals, shrine rituals, performing arts, and modern ensemble performances. Composed of 和 (Japanese) + 太鼓 (drum).

examples.japanese: {和太鼓|わだいこ}の{音|おと}が{響|ひび}いた。
examples.english: The sound of the Japanese drum echoed.

examples.japanese: {祭|まつ}りで{和太鼓|わだいこ}の{演奏|えんそう}を{聴|き}いた。
examples.english: I listened to a taiko performance at the festival.

examples.japanese: {和太鼓|わだいこ}は{全身|ぜんしん}を{使|つか}って{打|う}つので、{体力|たいりょく}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: Playing taiko requires physical strength since you use your whole body.

notes:
USAGE:
{和太鼓|わだいこ} distinguishes Japanese drums from Western drums (ドラム). In casual speech, {太鼓|たいこ} alone often refers to Japanese drums when the context is clear.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {和太鼓|わだいこ}を{打|う}つ / {叩|たた}く (to play/beat a taiko)
- {和太鼓|わだいこ}の{演奏|えんそう} (taiko performance)
- {和太鼓|わだいこ}グループ (taiko group/ensemble)
- {和太鼓|わだいこ}{体験|たいけん} (taiko experience/workshop)

CULTURAL NOTE:
{和太鼓|わだいこ} performance has evolved from traditional festival music into a modern performing art. Groups like {鼓童|こどう} have brought {和太鼓|わだいこ} to international audiences. Ensemble taiko ({組太鼓|くみだいこ}) as a stage art form developed primarily in the postwar period.
